I want to share a little of my story with you - but first, I have to ask...
#### **[Will you chip in $5 or $10 to my grassroots campaign today? The LAST public fundraising deadline before my primary is tomorrow, and we still need another 4,071 contributions to hit our goal!](https://substack.com/redirect/7d1b4b1c-2a43-4e67-abbc-d0102bc82783?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ DONATE](https://substack.com/redirect/7d1b4b1c-2a43-4e67-abbc-d0102bc82783?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Alright, back to my story...
I grew up on Andrews Air Force Base. My dad served, and our family believed in duty, honor, and community. Not as words on a wall, but as a code you actually live by.
I went on to play offensive lineman in college. On the line, your job isn't to be the star player -- it's to protect the people around you. Block. Hold the line. Make sure nobody gets through.
**I didn 't know it then, but I was training for everything that came next.**
I was working as a Capitol Police Officer on January 6th, 2021, when a violent mob stormed the building to overturn an election and destroy our democracy.
I was terrified, but I didn't run. I stood my ground. I defended this country, because that's what you do when it's your turn to answer the call. You don't think about it. You don't weigh the odds. You just do your job.
That's me. I'm not a career politician, and I'm not a millionaire. I'm a dad, a kid from a military family, a public servant, and a Marylander who thinks we deserve better.
Now I'm running for Congress - _and the other side is terrified._
Shady outside groups are pouring nearly **$5 MILLION** into this race to stop me. They're desperate to keep a regular guy like me out of the halls of Congress.
#### **[So please, help me fight back, win this race, and flip the House blue by chipping in $5 or $10 before tomorrow's deadline:](https://substack.com/redirect/7d1b4b1c-2a43-4e67-abbc-d0102bc82783?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

Together in the fight,
Harry Dunn

name: Voter Action Project
subject: Flat out lies
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Integrity First Voter Action Project, www
body:
Opponents of voting rights lack the common sense to understand that these anti-voting conspiracy theories are just flat-out lies. They'd rather see a vast web of shadowy interests arrayed against them than reexamine their own values when they lose elections.
That's why they create bills like the SAVE America, SAVE, and MEGA Acts, to strip our fundamental right to vote until only their select few have the privilege to vote.
Step up with $35 or more right now to stop the SAVE Act and defend our right to vote from these vicious attacks >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=060226_3&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
NYT: Trump Leans on Congress to Address His False Claims of Voter Fraud [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=060226_3&amount=25]
President Trump used his recent State of the Union address and the DHS funding debate to press Congress to advance stalled legislation that purports to address his often-repeated -- and equally debunked -- claims of widespread election fraud. There are stats from the conservative, right-wing Heritage Foundation below that prove it.
The SAVE America Act was fast-tracked by opponents of voting rights and passed the U.S. House of Representatives. Now Trump and his MAGA minions are meeting with U.S. Senators, scheming for ways to get this bill through the Senate ahead of November's midterms.
This bill is a stunning assault on our fundamental right to vote, and we can not afford to let this anti-democratic legislation become law, folks.
PITCH IN $35 RIGHT NOW TO STOP THE SAVE AMERICA ACT NOW ➜ [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=060226_3&amount=35]
Don’t be fooled by the name. This bill would force every voter to present specific types of proof of citizenship to register -- something millions of eligible Americans don’t have on hand. And that’s the point. The bill would also obliterate popular methods of voter registration for all voters, including:
* Registration by mail

* 3rd party voter registration drives

* Online voter registration in states that allow it

* Automatic voter registration
Some estimates say that this bill could disenfranchise up to 11 million eligible Americans , especially women and those who live in under-resourced communities.
“ There’s never been an attack on voting rights out of Congress like this ,” said Alexander Keyssar, a professor of History and Social Policy at the Harvard Kennedy School, and a leading historian of voting rights. “ It’s always been the federal government trying to keep states in check on voting rights, for the most part. ”
Team, the consequences of a bill like this passing would be catastrophic for our democracy. Chip in with $35 or whatever you can today to stop the SAVE AMERICA Act and other voter suppression bills from becoming law >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=060226_3&amount=35]
If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:
GIVE $15 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=060226_3&amount=15] GIVE $25 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=060226_3&amount=25] GIVE $50 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=060226_3&amount=50]
GIVE $100 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=060226_3&amount=100] GIVE $250 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=060226_3&amount=250] OTHER AMOUNT [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=060226_3&amount=35]
How do we know non-citizen voting is a made up problem? Because red states and conservative-leaning institutions have spent millions in taxpayer money and donor dollars searching for it and finding minimal results.
For example: The pro-Trump Heritage Foundation -- an organization that has funded anti-voting initiatives for decades -- maintains a database of "election crimes." Their own records only list 24 instances of non-citizens voting in U.S. elections from 2003 to 2023 . In other words -- 20 years of elections, millions of votes, and only 24 alleged non-citizen voters.
Reuters has a fuller accounting in recent reporting. Florida, for example, spent millions investigating voter fraud and creating a new state department to oversee election security. They've only prosecuted two non-citizens for voting since 2022. North Carolina said they found nine non-citizens registered to vote out of 7.7 million voters. Utah recently investigated their entire voter roll of 2.1 million registered voters and found one registered non-citizen who never attempted to vote.
The conservative CATO Institute says it best: " These investigations affirm what is simply common sense. People largely aren’t willing to risk their status in the United States — the land of economic opportunity — for the ability to cast one more vote out of hundreds of thousands or millions in a state and hundreds of millions in the country. "
Team, the lies aren't going to stop, but we can push back and make sure bills like this abomination never pass. Pitch in $35 or however much you can to stand against voter suppression bills in Congress and beyond >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=060226_3&amount=35]

It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities.

name: Josh Turek
subject: I’m Josh Turek and I’m the nominee to replace Joni Ernst in Iowa.
body:
[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260602_4.OXtgld&refcode=em20260602-4&t=1001&akid=6980%2E582294%2EAoWIkZ ]Josh Turek

I’m Josh Turek. I’m a Democratic state legislator who won a deep red seat,
four-time Paralympian, and two-time gold medalist in wheelchair
basketball.

I thought the feeling of winning my first gold medal at the 2016 Rio
Paralympics would only come once in a lifetime. But, the race was just
called:

I’m officially the Democratic nominee for Iowa’s open U.S. Senate seat.

Grassroots
energy usually peaks in the first few days after a primary, so we have to
get down to business ASAP. [ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260602_4.OXtgld&refcode=em20260602-4&t=1002&akid=6980%2E582294%2EAoWIkZ ]Will you help me make the most of our
hard-fought victory by splitting a donation between my campaign and Chris
Pappas to become one of the first Founding Donors of my General Election
campaign?

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260602_4.OXtgld&amount=5&refcode=em20260602-4&t=1003&akid=6980%2E582294%2EAoWIkZ ]Split a donation »

I’m honored that the people of Iowa have put their faith in me, and I’m
ready to take this once-in-a-generation shot to win this OPEN seat and be
the champion working people deserve in Washington.

I got into this race because like millions of fellow Democrats, I was fed
up with losing, fed up with treating “red” states like lost causes and
tired of perpetually playing defense.

I won this primary because I played offense, and I’m going to run a
relentless full-court press to win this seat in November.

I don’t take a penny of corporate PAC money. Your support, and your
support alone, will help us flip Iowa blue for the first time in more than
a decade and take back the Senate Majority.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260602_4.OXtgld&refcode=em20260602-4&t=1004&akid=6980%2E582294%2EAoWIkZ ]I’m personally asking you to become one of our first General Election
Founding Donors by splitting a contribution of $15, $20, $35, or more
today. Your contribution will power my voter outreach so I can flip Joni
Ernst’s Senate seat and restore hope and faith in the great state of Iowa.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260602_4.OXtgld&amount=5&refcode=em20260602-4&t=1005&akid=6980%2E582294%2EAoWIkZ ]Split a donation »

Look, I’m
under no illusions about the work it’ll take to win a battleground Senate
race as a Democrat in Iowa. Taking on Joni Ernst, Ashley Hinson, and their
billionaire-fueled MAGA Machine will be a beast of a challenge —
physically, mentally, financially.

But I’m not your average career politician. I’ve won back-to-back
victories in deep red Trump country. Polls show me either tied with or one
point ahead of my official Republican opponent, Ashley Hinson.

This election will be a nail-biter, and it starts right now.

We have 153 days to bring independents and conservatives into our Prairie
Populist coalition; to overcome over $40 million in spending from MAGA
megadonors; and to let the world know that working-class Americans own the
future.

Ads, statewide tours, and campaign infrastructure don’t come cheap, and
our campaign coffers are nearly empty after a hard-fought and high-cost
primary victory.

The outcome of this race will decide the Senate majority with huge
implications for our country, so my team and I need every single solitary
ounce of support to hit the ground rolling. [ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260602_4.OXtgld&refcode=em20260602-4&t=1006&akid=6980%2E582294%2EAoWIkZ ]Will you rush a split
contribution to become one of my first General Election Founding Donors in
this high-stakes Senate race ASAP?

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260602_4.OXtgld&amount=5&refcode=em20260602-4&t=1025&akid=6980%2E582294%2EAoWIkZ ]Donate $5 »

We have a ton of work to do and history to make here in Iowa.

Let's do this.

Talk soon,

Josh Turek

You can unsubscribe from this mailing list at any time:
http://act.chrispappas.org/cms/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?akid=6980%2E582294%2EAoWIkZ

body:
Are you ready, New Mexico?!

| | | [](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/134?t=1&akid=10079%2E400544%2ETnksLz)

[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/10403?refcode=jtk809-fr-nd&t=2&akid=10079%2E400544%2ETnksLz)
**I am officially the Democratic nominee for Governor of New Mexico!**
| | [Chip in to keep this incredible momentum going](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/10403?refcode=jtk809-fr-nd&t=3&akid=10079%2E400544%2ETnksLz)

This is a huge milestone, friend — and it's one I couldn't have reached without you. **_Thank you._**

I’m a daughter of Pueblo women, a New Mexican, a single mother, and a former small business owner. I’ve served as a Congresswoman and became the first Native American Cabinet Secretary in U.S. history. **_[And when we win this race in November, I will be the first Native American woman elected Governor in any state.](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/10403?refcode=jtk809-fr-nd&t=4&akid=10079%2E400544%2ETnksLz)_**
Thanks to supporters like you, we're now one step closer to delivering for working families and making our vision of a New Mexico for New Mexicans a reality.
But there’s still a long road to November, and Republicans are already watching to see whether we can keep this momentum going – ready to spend anything to bring their extremist agenda here.
Our campaign has always been about New Mexicans building something together. I am ready to deliver stronger schools, affordable childcare and housing, higher wages, support for small businesses, better healthcare access, and safer communities. The general election is about more than what we stand to lose. It’s about what we stand to gain.
So, are you ready New Mexico?

Are you ready to fight for lower costs?

Are you ready to fight for healthcare?

Are you ready to fight for safe communities?

Are you ready to fight for education?

Are you ready to show Donald Trump and his administration that, here in New Mexico, we believe in dignity and respect?
I’m ready to lead New Mexico forward. I’ve lived the challenges working families are facing and taken on tough fights to deliver real results. I know what it takes to win in November — but I can’t do it alone: **_[So please, will you chip in to help me hit our first $50,000 general election goal, win this November, and keep New Mexico blue?](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/10403?refcode=jtk809-fr-nd&t=5&akid=10079%2E400544%2ETnksLz)_**

subject: Oklahoma Gov. Candidate Jake Merrick Has Record of Mismanaging Campaign Funds and Personal Fina
body:
| | [](https://112138.io.directiq14.com/hit?sid=688v5qad5empzrulmv9&linkid=0&link=59ee30b6d9b046139be60cd64c1c30a9)
---
| **Oklahoma Gov. Candidate Jake Merrick Has Record of Mismanaging Campaign Funds and Personal Financial Woes** [](https://112138.io.directiq14.com/hit?sid=688v5qad5empzrulmv9&linkid=1&link=d5ed4610e8ea45cfaecca24a3ba948e5) In the crowded 2026 Republican primary for Oklahoma governor, podcaster and former state senator Jake Merrick [positions himself as a fiery populist outsider](https://112138.io.directiq14.com/hit?sid=688v5qad5empzrulmv9&linkid=2&link=96ebe10fd5d84e099bfd328c350c3838), championing faith, family, and freedom against the political establishment through his grassroots-style campaign along Route 66. Yet beneath the authentic image lies serious trouble: Merrick faces significant financial problems and campaign mismanagement issues that raise doubts about his ability to lead effectively as governor. Many of Merrick's supporters are shocked about the newly exposed history of personal financial mismanagement and the ethical issues it raises. Elected to office in a 2021 special election to finish Stephanie Bice's term in Senate District 22 after she won her U.S. House seat, Merrick billed himself as a brash outsider, defeating Democrat Molly Ooten with about 65% of the vote after besting fellow Republican Keri Shipley in the primary election. Sworn in on April 14, 2021, he positioned himself as a fresh conservative voice. Voters quickly experienced buyer's remorse. In the 2022 Republican primary, Edmond business owner Kristen Thompson challenged him. On June 28, 2022, she defeated the incumbent Merrick decisively. His time in the Senate lasted just over a year. Most concerning are his uses of campaign funds. Records show reimbursements for personal expenses, including artwork and frames from Hobby Lobby, clothes, tables, lights, cleaning supplies, and Halloween candy. He spent $815 on suits and pants with campaign money and had questionable cash disbursements totaling around $1,500. In late 2021, he used at least $1,997.64 in campaign funds for podcast equipment, effectively building his media brand on donor dollars. After losing the primary, Merrick directed $1,279.58 from his campaign to his nonprofit, Paraklete Inc., whose financials are not readily available to the public. In summer 2022, he reimbursed himself over $1,000, including a notable $948 just after the July 4 holiday. Aggravating matters further, campaign finance records from that period also expose the gap between Merrick's rhetoric and reality. He campaigned against special interests but accepted thousands in PAC donations: $7,500 in January 2021, $5,000 in February/March, another $1,000 in late March, and $5,500 during his failed 2022 re-election bid. _**One of the campaign filings showing that the Merrick campaign received PAC funds.**_ As senator, he reported accepting $976.50 in free meals from lobbyists--dozens of wining-and-dining sessions that contradict his outsider image. _**Merrick was frequently wined and dined by lobbyists during his time as state senator.**_ Merrick has apparently not reformed his profligate ways since 2022. Recent reports show [Merrick spending beyond his contributions](https://112138.io.directiq14.com/hit?sid=688v5qad5empzrulmv9&linkid=3&link=09236e77782849329a17e333890fa755), landing in a serious deficit--despite railing against PAC and lobbyist money. Merrick attributed discrepancies to reporting errors but the optics echo his short stint in the State Senate. "I initially decided to vote for Jake Merrick for Governor," one Oklahoma housewife told the National News Brief. "Now I wonder how he could manage a multibillion dollar state budget if he can't handle his own personal finances? Jake Merrick turns out not to be the person he says he is." Evidently, Merrick is also having problems paying his residential mortgage. A recent lawsuit initiated by Great Plains National Bank against Merrick highlights the depths of his personal financial woes. Great Plains National Bank is [seeking $10,000 in debts](https://112138.io.directiq14.com/hit?sid=688v5qad5empzrulmv9&linkid=4&link=e0e224c6f90442368e400af965118fda) owed by Merrick and his wife, Nicole, over what they describe as a delinquent mortgage. As Merrick is apparently having trouble paying his bills, he is mounting a run for Governor--perhaps believing the position would be a panacea that could help his ongoing financial woes. _**The lawsuit filed against Merrick and his wife over an alleged delinquent mortgage.**_ Oklahomans tuning into Merrick's podcasts hear a compelling populist conservative. But peering behind the microphone reveals someone who, when given power, quickly began accepting perks, blurring lines between campaign and personal expenses, and failing to earn re-election from the voters who sent him to the Senate very quickly after his initial election. Oklahoma faces real challenges: education, taxes, infrastructure, and preserving conservative values amid a federal government that remains massive and obtrusive even as President Trump works diligently to bring about reform. The state needs steady, trustworthy leadership, not another smooth talker whose record suggests the people of Oklahoma would be highly disappointed if he were able to flim-flam his way into the Governorship. **Good Morning!** On this day in 1888, the baseball poem _[Casey at the Bat](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFurDAQheGngQ5kj30NFC5uQ7dpU1oGj5dJbIzw7K54-2jzCumPPun8nzd385Rov3_4jJZjcTu-akJmPB2fj3x8U0pVjgulRGWPjz347ECA6YTphHLBU7qcboONiICqRSuHUehRKq3bzWoMkwywRABhJiVDjALiGE2EKfzzpiX71oQRSgoxCd0vox9wGCSuyuME2GiBgbic_VehnTeM6SpPPPu15DbZjfmojfrfwNzATHssfb4q01rZ5-M9amBefcWr89zxht3i2XGgrYG5PW04Xu9v1QyNFvfsKf3C_KcaTws_AQAA__9O0nQg),_ penned by Ernest Lawrence Thayer, was first published in the San Francisco _ Daily Examiner_, with its famous final line (spoiler alert!): _" But there is no joy in Mudville--mighty Casey has struck out."_ A little fish in Texas and Mexico has thrived for 100,000 years without a single male in sight, cloning itself generation after generation. Scientists thought the all-female Amazon molly should have died out ages ago, but she's still [swimming along just fine](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOpDAQRL8GMqO24cAEDi4hm0svRAa3B9-18chuBrFfv2K1f7AVlVRSVen9fcwPGyjszz82omGf5h3PQsiMeeZ8xNf_QFSkXgJRSLs_dmfjrED1AnoB7exsoGvuamc8osK2RiMHDZ2WbdfVm1kXcN5rv2ocpVNK6xHw1-ix7z3Ytq-Dudugh1YCjNA1i7YDDoPEtbU4Kqw6QBc45eZfCjtv6OlKb8zNmmJNZmN-lar9XampUtN5ns2yrHdWqckffGSs1GQzh5Vu9z0mhY32I-0iJqJL8IbCh7IJ3iwXQeGNTviUhYRb4kKbizgDb-lgES1hqbNxr_PGUvqh6uAZbaCvT_wjkG-jPgMAAP__sq6HtA), as we explain in today's _Science_ section. ## Trump Kills $1.8 Billion 'Lawfare' Fund
President Trump's administration is scrapping its roughly [$1.8 billion](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLtu4zAQRb-G6mSMSOpVsNhGnbfdUhhJQ2s2fAgkbcP5-kBOlTr1Ae7FOf-u8xXZcbj9RU-m2DgHemZHpVCaS7r744Ody82wsHMcg72HDf0sQXY1dDWoeUN2r1lXm7FEklRFpukH0EOjtK52Y2FYWySrurGB1Q7SqlbhIge76GVpqGJzrkEHqgEYQV-WAXvq-4ZWhTRKEhpo4xLT5X_kUHay7hUflC5r9JUzeylHFuqPkJOQU9lpZ-dOJuS0R0-nkJATbp4D55KwcAxCTu0Iuh11_basf-I6rwmPXGMoXD8Jjxj485ucBYScqmS243lGyV0vNNw88vu1Kr_K-DDyKwAA__8LA4ln) "anti-weaponization" fund, which would have paid people who say they were wrongly targeted by the Justice Department, acting Attorney General Todd Blanche told Congress Tuesday. The money came from [settling Trump's lawsuit](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0D1uhDAQBeDTmM7If4uhcJGGbtOmRAOMl9kYG4FZtDl95Fwh3Ugjvafvfd2HO1Cg-PiEFV32aYh4HQFzxn3I-7lu3xTCIduRQqAU_RlnWAclVMNFw4UeZqDwHkw1O4-oUFfopG2FaaU2plrcaKRHb2GCRmvlR_DWttB03e02eWmhIlfSRCO0FKITph5bsGitxEkDdgqZEThTTnv9TBTzgj680wv3ekprFdyS83Yw_cFUz1R_XVc9jUdRlD9TfTmZ6scAcVqQz-nJIWbiF8KWIv1AphR5gfElnQcy1Ve7m7eriI_GMiMeK1D4q8v_2ujl1G8AAAD__zYZfMw) against the IRS over the leak of his tax returns. "_We are not moving forward with the fund, period,"_ Blanche said. The plan had drawn criticism from both parties, and [Senate Republicans](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOozAQBuCnMZ3RYBsMhYtr6HLtlWjAQzK3xkbGCco-_Yq8wnYjjfT_-v5_t-mGHDje_-JGrqxpinQegUqhPJX83PYvDuFo-plD4BTXZ_S4TQpUJ6GToCePHN6TqbxbiRTpilxjezB9o42pHk5bXIA6GAbb6q5dWlxxWZWfbavBQF-xu9KgA90ADGDquUdL1ja0aKRBkTBAnkvK9f_EsTxoDe_0olwvaauCe5SyH0L_EWoUajzPs17m41Jcf6HG6xRq_GAkxsLyJNxT5G8snKK8SNLntO_kZab9OQdeMMpMrxSKUGOVnd_Py390Vhi4b8jhU15-tdjLqZ8AAAD__8dSgec) refused to pass the president's immigration funding bill until it was resolved. Two federal judges had also stepped in, with one [temporarily blocking](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD2upDAQhE8DmZGx_fgJHGxC9jbdEDV2M_SssZHdDJo9_Yq5wkurpFJ935_v-RsoUHz8hh0tr2mOeJWAzJhnzud-_KUQSjssFAKluJ7Rwz4rqTohOyH17IHCeza1tyuiQl2jbftBmqHVxtSb1WZZ2xHcANosX-NgFjXiYvxqWvC-g5rsvSY7qVspR2maZYAe-75FpwFHhZWR6IlTbp6JIm-4hnd6YW5c2utgN-ajVPpXpaZKTdd1NXFxN8XdV2o6UiAmVyo1Pc_C5FB4PCDzjpE_oX-g2CBwER9iAZFJXAhHivQPmFIUN7d4QhSdOHIq6E5OWawUsIhyEovsImjTf-mxztYf162rdH1l5GMHCp-v_CPBL6v-BwAA__81DJOA) the fund and another reopening the IRS case to examine whether the settlement was collusive. Critics had warned it could pay people charged over the Jan. 6 protest.
## California Awaits Results from Tuesday's Vote
California held its primary Tuesday, but the [tight governor's race](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL1ygzAMgJ_GbHDCJhgGD13Y0rUj52A5USpszjbJ5e179OcJumnQJ333fZznsyWmcH23K5ri4xzwmRlLwTSXtK_bJzHndrgQM8Xg9-DsOkuQfQ19DWp2lvg1d5UzHlGiqtC0eoBuaFXXVTczupOCVp9A6ZMeVO88aClbPzqPSsNSkTmuQQ-qBRihay6D1ah1i4uyOEoUHaCjElNzjxTKDT2_4gNTs8S1YnMrZctCvQk5CTktlld72OcmpquQ0xaZCi1ZyAkZl0IxHPPxU8gJ-h-GfEyBbL0lWm161X-rdcK8c8n1fQ9Y_0JVMm57HkFyr0UH19USf9uUfyV8GPkVAAD__3zuhJA) could take days or even weeks to call. Mail ballots postmarked by Election Day are counted through June 9. Democrats Xavier Becerra, a former federal health secretary, and billionaire Tom Steyer are battling Republican Steve Hilton for the two spots that advance to the [general election](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGunDAQRb_GdEaDbWEoXKSh27Qp0QBjdhJjI9u7aP8-4hXvB143misd3Xv-POYHcuC4_8aDXPVpjnSVQLVSnmt-Hec_DqF0w8IhcIr-FTc8ZgWql9BL0POGHD6zaTbniRTphlxnBzBDp41pnm6wYEkrtaleg9KLGf0wdj1pD2C9pobdTYMedAcwgmmXAS1Z29GqkUZFwgBtXFNu_yaO9Uk-fNKbcrumownuWetZhP4l1CTUdF1Xuy7lXnHnQk33KdR0Zj4wMxW5YmCfcmSU-82JKReZcSUZUpEYdwpU5IGf7z-nC4Wamuy287pFlN4KA_uBHL5a1B-pezv1PwAA__-5gIRl). More than 60 candidates ran to replace term-limited Gov. Gavin Newsom. No Republican has won a statewide race in California since 2006. In another big race, Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass faced [a surprisingly strong challenge](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkE1ugzAQhU9jdkTjsQtm4UWliq6SbZdogCFxO-DIdhJx-4peodv3pPfzfZ2HMwUJ2_VCK_uyxGHjVxYuhdNQ0mO9_wSRrN0YRELclsc20zogYFNDU4MZZgqyD7aa_cKMbCr2unVgnTbWVjc_Mlty-m2axmWEyeoOEFokBw6p464K_kiDBowG6MCeRkctt63myRB3yMoCz6HEdPqOYSs3XmSPT06nKa6V-Fsp96zMu8JeYU_jdDw4PIX95_mQL_zKCnuJuabtysK5XmmPiaRm4amEuNXHBoV9LjHtyvRhVuZDG2MdOtNVyc_310EgN62ycF0pyF99-Rezp8ffAAAA___oLH4n) from GOP candidate Spencer Pratt. Voters in five other states also picked nominees Tuesday, including Iowa, where Democrats chose Josh Turek [to face Rep. Ashley Hinson](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOrCAYhZ8GOwwgohYUt7Gb225pfvV3YAbBAA5xn37jvsJ2JznJl3O-r8f0AOusf_6HHXXewuSxJIc5Y5xyPPfjbZ1LvJ-tczb47fQr7JNgQlGmKGumFay7JlmtekMU2FSoedcz2fNGysrolS0geNt2apn7XrQtCJBs42rgQs3tVll905hiDWdsYLKee-iw6zguDeAgkEiGq80h1q9gfTa4uSt8MNZL2CunTc5HIs0_IkYixlJKvczpfnH3RIx3JGK0oQBN6CEjPaLdIV40YjpdThSScXhRY30Knr5CMjSfEd_0GxZDCxh3E6qo16PcHpLqiGTPHaz7HZH_ZO6jxU8AAAD__5YZhGs), the winner of the Republican primary for the state's open U.S. Senate seat.
## Remote Work, Not AI, Hitting Young Grads
The rise of remote work, not artificial intelligence, explains most of the recent jump in joblessness among young college graduates, according to a [new analysis](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2u4yAUhJ8Gd1hwQJgUFNu4y7ZbWtgcEhJ-LCCx_PYr31e49Ugz833_7svdhhjy469NaLovS8ajRewd69LrJ-3vEGPjeg0xhpL9JzubFmCgKFOUicXZEM9FDs54REAxoOGTZlJzIeXwNP62gmNKgJPWWtwU56C40Ay817jqIZirjSkmOGM3JsdV2wmnieMmLN4AiWToQi91fJWQ-xN9PMsX67iVNETz7H1vRPwhMBOYj-MY9zPl3q6YwIxbySWdBOZrhsCcT-rRUR-ya7RiKh3pUeqb5tKpDfQCRkcx93rSiF-M9FXWRmAeqnH7cYloaiKSPZIN8edF_5W6r4H_AQAA__-vdoOD) from the Federal Reserve Bank of New York. Employers say they're filling work-from-home jobs with [experienced hires](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDuOwyAYhE-DOyxeMU5BsY27bLulheEnZsPDwjjIt185V9hmmk_6RjM_j_mhffDp-a0jqOrynKDtAWqFMtdyxO3lQ9jpuPgQfE7uSFbHmRE2YDJgwmerfThn0VnlABjwDhSVIxEj5UJ0qzLcWssHI8DCQC23VEp9E-ZO3M1RzjqvLhsZCKeE3Inol1FLkJKC4RruDJAgYH3Npf_NPtUVXDjzG0pvcuyCWmvddsS_EJsQm1prvUmLuSBi06VGbCKfoIhNBWKugFsuL3zmo674SBC3kM8IqeIEDZ8Xc2D7tcbQFWW3do3fB4kEeUbtw6e5_uuut2J_AQAA__8ogH6U) rather than fresh grads because of the difficulty of training someone over long distance. Unemployment among graduates under 29 rose from 3.1% before the pandemic to 3.7%, even as the rate for older, seasoned workers [slipped](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLtuwzAMRb9G3mxQj_oxaOiiLVnaougkKBaVqNHDsOUY-ftC-YUuXIhD3nu-T_pkfPDpejYRZXFZJzy2gKXgqsu6x-XuQ9joePEh-JzcnqyJmgHrW-hb4NoaH55aNFY6RIa8QUmHEcRIuRDNTfLJWNq_iQsOhjsHkxOTG2cqxnmaBxgbL-s16IFTgAlEdxnNgMNAceYGJ4ZEAFpf8tr9Zp_KDV145geu3ZxjE-StlGUj_J0wRZg6jqPbF193hKnPvOgzHhth6uuDMFU_EabgNShh6vzTKrTtijEXbINPd7TtnjAuIT8jplIhQWsjLibWV7BZpV2O6mPrByLgGo0PrzDlXwYfkv0FAAD__4-9gKs). The findings push back on a popular theory that AI is wiping out entry-level roles, though the authors caution that this could change as the technology spreads.

## Court Clears Texas App Age Law
Texas' law requiring age verification on app stores is now in effect after [the Fifth Circuit's ruling](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGSpCAURb8GM7oAFeyAYBOz2XRDC_GhrxrFgjfS8_db7S9MfOreOvf--5q-HEY81r9uB0vvkKYDaolABHkq53cuV3kd6F-F4O3KnNJOqU5KKM2F5qKdFofxZ-qaxc5iecoGrDSD6IauF6bZrNeDlP0Ag9RKPo1ZQGsVnvOsuwGM7xu0nzKhRSulkF3_MN0AQppW6dmLRRvWCViQUn7QBrdFiD_pgvzwaW-i3YjOwto_TI1MjbXWx-vtjg9kavysYWq8Y0yNAQNt3GP230g8AhV-I-7Ok7sV-AUZA3pHmA4eXeVr4nhQ4hACeOIhZX6kytTYZLucFWPEcjuuu8N4K9Hvjrys-h8AAP__yEOKAA) stayed an injunction that had blocked it since December. [Senate Bill 2420](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGurCAQBuCn0Y4NIqJbUNzGbm97SwPMrJJFxgCuu29_ozlvcLrJZObPl__fY3oYH3yc_5oVdfk8aYp45IClYJrytqf8zq_o3SsX_JhsidZCxyS4UIwrxtsJjA_fSdagLYd7U6Nu-oHLQXa8rxftQFlhLXTg8K64BYumlyD7QXSNsl3t9RnGFW-bhjeyu_VyQN70rVDWcVB9JTmCL5RuZcFL8QxfemO6OVrroJdStly1fyoxVmI8-TKbaGKh6Om8-dlWYgzkTKjEeKUwM7PDx8zMtqEJmTnaU2FpP_tg-7ZQgHMyMzK3oHtl9qTEVh8pXU8M6IiBDOQ6adgOH4LPl3dejQ8Xr_yu1LcW_wMAAP__d2OQ1g), signed by Gov. Greg Abbott in May 2025, requires Apple, Google, and other app store operators to verify the ages of all users. Minors need parental consent before downloading any app or making in-app purchases. Attorney General Ken Paxton had appealed the December injunction, and the Fifth Circuit's stay is [temporary pending an appeal](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGStCAQhJ9GMyxABf-A4E_M9tILLZTBpRYdC-Zk9-2v9BUununur_v7MT1siGFfv-wGht4epx1KjkAEacrHT8pnfu1heWWCt80z4kZYJsmlYlwx3k7OhviZutqZmbt_ogYj9MC7oeu5rp9GqF4LLrrB9UpJcG03WJDW6XYZhJ19HcxlxhVvxfXXN7obgAvdSjUv3ClddRxcIEwNPeGm8PGDJ6Rmwa2O5kl05Kr9X8mxkmMppXml9byOlRyvNpUcbxmzx8HsCuyEFHxYLAXcWbSF2RixgGOEbEUWdkIG3sNCzGNiO5Y6GXeUEGPIN9C62RDvfPrbaqeRvwEAAP__NBKDyQ). Tech industry groups are challenging the law's constitutionality under the First Amendment.
## Texas CDL Rules Shift Two Ways
Texas made back-to-back commercial driver's license policy changes Monday: mandating [English-only written exams](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLvOozAQhZ_GdI7GY3MrKLah-7fdEvkyJFYMRngSwtuvwiv87TnSp_Odfz_Tj40prve_dqGBP3OeVjpKImbap7K99vIuzzX6Z2H62OJyXjgfEwI2EhoJego2pnMyVRgchF5VNKi2A9OZGtrqMXToQTtS0AZrELyeSfcQ5s570wQTqjh8YdCAVgqUqW-t6QhUq7FxHkLTCgMUIuf9xg-6VszpzG_abz4vVRoezFsR-o_AUeB4HMft-X7RtxQ42p2jTyRw_HoJHFP2NgkcL5DA0YckmQoXeSUyzzPtFGRe0ylpvadYHjLQZndeaGW5vVyKXhY7E58CR2x62aCfa-eUVIG0NL3ysnedlcHXtauV7kjZah_CdsSUYrmU7ouN6TLg3_3-HvB_AAAA___xe5gC) while simultaneously reopening a credential program for H-2A agricultural workers. The Department of Public Safety announced that CDL and learner permit knowledge tests [are now English-only](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLvSpCAUhJ9GM6wj4i0g2MTs33RDC-Go1HCZ4jDDzNtv6Sv8WQfdXV_3v5_1R1lnw_FXeZT5s8c1YCGHOWNa6flK9KZHsPpBGT-Kthh9jmXlwAcGA4NuNcq67ypqIzcwc1ujbMcJxCR6GOtTmmHstBl66Pepmzczaz5zwQFUu827ErWVVxkM0LUttKJvRjEhtGPHh02DGcZKABqbY2ryiTfF7r7xjanR0ddOnjk_qer-VHyp-FJKafb4EdeMy1Dx5ZIVX-4o8yoYlZEYhsNZOlkM7su0cSwjZWIJ6eWRmLMaA9lwMEJFMSjHdpU8KzE9MFGdpHkW65ylm_DwyrobKP_uxrfk_wMAAP__0tWLNg), effective June 1. The change doesn't affect the hands-on skills test, which has always been English-only. Hours later, DPS reversed course on a separate restriction, reinstating [non-domiciled CDLs for H-2A workers](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGyqyAQxvGn0Q5nBQOmoLiN3bntLR2ETWSC4LAoydvfia9w-v_s_Pb79zP_GB98fP41G-ryfqQ5YqWApWCeaT8ynfSK3r6o4NvQktJWUp05cMlAMhCzMz585qF1egF371vUvRphGIcbqHbVxvA7d0LdeA93a6UBJWC0ToIRFhfZev09BhJE30M_3Do1jAi9ElwuFpxUzQDofEm5Kyteikf4pBNzZ9PWBr2WslMj_jR8avhUa-3cTt0Vds90Nnz6vtTwye3ETIzpiBaJZaRj24tPkcUUmUubtz6gY9YF5okOc2Ur44bVlF-Yqc3a7dWH4OliPTfjw6Uov9vu1Px_AAAA___QQoam) under updated federal guidelines. Eligible workers with current licenses may continue using them until expiration. Those with expired credentials may file to have their credentials renewed. The resumption follows a Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration rule change that took effect in March. H-2A applicants must appear in person at a DPS Driver License Office with all required documents.
## Spurs Return to NBA Finals
San Antonio is back on basketball's biggest stage for the first time in 12 years, hosting the New York Knicks in Game 1 of the [NBA Finals](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGypCAURL8GMywERAwINjF7m25oIVxHalAsLyPj32-N8wkv7q6uc_rfz_hjQwzb469dweT3nMYNCkbIGY4R99eBJz634J6Y4W1xSmnNqYyccUWZokyM3oZ4jbLyZmK-byowTaeZ1LJlXbWYefI9aKFaDkLx2Unfaq_6hlmpNQBUwXzGmGKiaVgj27qTGljTCa4mx7zqiGTgQ05HnRe4KeZ4pROO2qW1imbJeUci_hA-ED6UUmrAffuEhA_bZAkfMKfjInwYCR-CJ3yQuhc9F_rboHPYbER6W93S9OtM9wPOAIU-4UIKb3CvHE5A6pJ1CyBFl14Zq8P4vYQYA964j9WGeNPl3316Gv4_AAD__9dkjF8) tonight at the Frost Bank Center. Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | Today's Top Pick (ads) | • | Salem Media Group ---|--- • | Research Boulevard • | Weiss Ratings Plus | | | Market Commentary Disclaimer We encourage all readers to consult a qualified financial professional — such as a registered investment adviser or licensed broker — before making any investment decision. # FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
June 3, 2026

CONTACT:
Todd Cheewing
516.521.7926
[Todd@Ascent-Strategic.com](mailto:Todd@Ascent-Strategic.com)

LILY TANG WILLIAMS EARNS ENDORSEMENT FROM GUN OWNERS OF AMERICA

WEARE, N.H. — Republican congressional candidate Lily Tang Williams today announced that she has received the endorsement of Gun Owners of America (GOA), one of the nation's leading grassroots Second Amendment organizations. Gun Owners of America endorsed Williams based on her unwavering commitment to defending Granite Staters’ Second Amendment rights.

_"I truly am honored to receive the endorsement of Gun Owners of America,"_ said Lily Tang Williams. _"As someone who grew up under communism, I understand firsthand that the right to self-defense is a fundamental safeguard of liberty.”_

Gun Owners of America praised Williams' commitment to supporting policies that defend the rights of responsible firearm owners. Throughout her campaign, Williams has emphasized individual liberty, limited government, and strict adherence to the Constitution. GOA stated: “Lily earned GOA’s support because she will oppose any new gun control laws and will work to roll back unconstitutional gun laws already on the books... [She] understands we don’t need politicians or government bureaucrats to control every aspect of our lives, including our ability to protect ourselves and our families.”

_"New Hampshire has a proud tradition of freedom and self-reliance,"_ Williams added. _"From populated to rural parts of the Second District, people understand that the Second Amendment maintains our cherished Live Free or Die spirit.”_

Gun Owners of America represents millions of gun owners nationwide and has long been recognized as one of the most influential organizations advocating for the protection of Second Amendment rights.

For more information about Lily Tang Williams and her campaign, visit [lily4congress.com](https://us.list-manage.com/qyHLHr6D_ly?e=c338950e03&c2id=adf8b61e01be85c238f26a96cfd7c41c).

About Lily Tang Williams

Born in China during Mao’s Cultural Revolution to working-class parents, Lily Tang Williams immigrated to the United States with nothing and built a life as an entrepreneur, educator, and community leader in Weare, NH. A living embodiment of the American Dream, she brings a uniquely powerful perspective to the fight for freedom and limited government.

In 2024, Williams won the Republican nomination and captured 47% of the general election vote against current incumbent Maggie Goodlander — coming closer than any Republican has in over a decade to flipping NH-02. She is back and running stronger than ever in 2026.

# **▶️: The Truth about Immigration...**
Recently, I received a _comment_ on one of my videos claiming that immigrants are responsible for terrorism and that our country is under threat because of who is crossing our borders.[**_Please watch the video below to hear my response and learn why facts—not fear—must guide our immigration policy._**](https://1xz3r.mjt.lu/lnk/AVwAAJvqk-4AAc7KuUYAA-Neh6MAAYKKXNoAoUWGADIMFwBqICAPct81ozcxSaCnSJ0x6DlA3AAtq28/2/cUgHz7VscNt2bzCUeABDaw/aHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuYWN0Ymx1ZS5jb20vZG9uYXRlL25vLW1pc2luZm8)
| [](https://1xz3r.mjt.lu/lnk/AVwAAJvqk-4AAc7KuUYAA-Neh6MAAYKKXNoAoUWGADIMFwBqICAPct81ozcxSaCnSJ0x6DlA3AAtq28/3/QoTvfA2J203CWZ8YHfk1Qw/aHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuYWN0Ymx1ZS5jb20vZG9uYXRlL25vLW1pc2luZm8)
---
**Let me be clear: fear is not a policy.** Fear does not secure our border. Fear does not make our communities safer.**Facts do. **Like many Americans, my family has an immigration story. I have shared that story in the past because**immigration is woven into the fabric of this country.** Generation after generation, people have come to America seeking opportunity, freedom, and a better life for their families. That story is not a weakness—it is one of our greatest strengths.None of this means we should ignore the challenges facing our immigration system. We need a system that is orderly, secure, and functional. We need leaders willing to address border security, modernize our immigration process, and enforce the law fairly and effectively. But we can do all of that without demonizing entire communities or turning neighbor against neighbor.[**_Division won't solve this problem. Honest leadership and practical solutions will--and I am committed to just that. Together, we can move Texas' 8th District forward. _**](https://1xz3r.mjt.lu/lnk/AVwAAJvqk-4AAc7KuUYAA-Neh6MAAYKKXNoAoUWGADIMFwBqICAPct81ozcxSaCnSJ0x6DlA3AAtq28/4/YVyTfrpi6LFzII-mbkwmDA/aHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuYWN0Ymx1ZS5jb20vZG9uYXRlL25vLW1pc2luZm8)

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. ## Red Wave Hits Deep-Blue California: Republicans Surge in Race to Replace Newsom
The bluest state in America just handed Republicans a result almost nobody saw coming. In Tuesday's all-party primary to replace term-limited Governor Gavin Newsom, Trump-endorsed commentator **Steve Hilton** battled to the front of a 60-plus candidate field, with early returns showing him in a dead heat at the top alongside Democrat Xavier Becerra.By Wednesday morning, with more than half the vote counted, Hilton had opened a narrow lead over Becerra — roughly **27% to 25%** — with billionaire Democrat Tom Steyer running third. Under California's jungle-primary rules, the top two advance to November regardless of party.What's Happening
* ▸ A field of **more than 60 candidates** splintered the Democratic vote, leaving the party's establishment scrambling.
* ▸ Days before the vote, the California Democratic Party held a press conference to **sound the alarm** after internal polling showed Republicans leading.
* ▸ Republican Riverside County Sheriff **Chad Bianco** also posted a strong showing, raising the once-unthinkable prospect of an all-GOP runoff in November.

Why It MattersA Republican hasn't won a California governor's race since Arnold Schwarzenegger. Hilton built his campaign on the issues working families actually feel — **gas prices, electric bills, vehicle fees, and a promise to make the first $100,000 of income tax-free.** When affordability becomes the ballgame, even California is in play.Read the full story at [The Washington Post](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/ss/c/u001.SfPhhFqVdCCzAqIAosiI_FBjDs6G1Gvuty5mEXWKH_GRLptpsuFeInwhdVS7_DyOCkvS1kPVmVEsBznx_XPbDUdMlbpd_2YHr4yqqeQK6KPcn5kGpcVn8xfkshVg84aQ4Rk9V4T8ms8XcBoqTMkdsHINQUk9BnTh1dy3LOIxg67e7mGbC7asEQuM2SnB_O8EfVnwxTlk64oWDheuLzT8iTIu1KtTDDNpeyBCYF-Rtw7o31ZpqpUBMpp4PVfCwOHY4iz0lGptlDixO7wKj4O5EsQ6ouhIr24EEwJIteld-7APJPuyPV5qw_RBmJivF2xBxit0txX1gfxWp1Zke5TnPomBpf532r8VERBjAfOabh3_A-I4zugNLJEnBAKXvitih4SQFXcLnNGXPgkNYO9NfA/4r6/w-bgnRmHS7Ci0CeQIFt0JA/h5/h001.XGj_iXuhgu9gGJBG84xa48BjfS1p2LbQUkFEjZnvQV4).

## Iowa Farmer Topples Washington Insider in Stunning GOP Upset
Grassroots conservatives in Iowa just sent a message to the political class: the endorsement game isn't everything. Businessman and farmer **Zach Lahn** edged out four-term Congressman Randy Feenstra in Tuesday's Republican gubernatorial primary, an outsider beating the establishment favorite.The Numbers
* ▸ With **99%** of the expected vote counted, Lahn led Feenstra **37.8% to 37%** — razor-thin, but enough.
* ▸ Feenstra **conceded** Tuesday night and threw his full support behind Lahn ahead of November.
* ▸ Lahn aligned himself with the **"Make America Healthy Again"** movement and picked up the backing of former Rep. Steve King.

The PerspectiveLahn ran on a message Iowans understood in their bones — he told supporters the state has **lost 10,000 family farms since 2000** while hedge funds and foreign buyers snap up the land. He'll face Democrat Rob Sand in a November race the GOP can't afford to take for granted, in a state Republicans have held since the George W. Bush era.Read the full story at [NBC News](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/ss/c/u001.SfPhhFqVdCCzAqIAosiI_Hww93iPI4LJrShhMJMeWsBwwLRkiqL8TVbHKcIylW_-RcSKHh4avkXMzm7QRbEIbn3wJq4LwXpaHpLYGgYlb__QIKdb1E8jC15IKIFiKv1P_sPGleRGn5EvI7MNanBizIQyWRJFP79HuZwxH3PsPx9rZ4kREc-gyxj770UFNvTXKhYrTXhjr6uCSSNhOkW1gEJ5mHjY8bVtcHhK1k3JfqRcDv0C1uy4j_0YwZjllS1J2W8Uf99nS-8lxUAfcRsM0hLST8s-Ztwh4EinCKdCSsyqovpssG9tGnfhtXXYstpPZn0Ppqsm475CDfniiGqGPYIeFfFJqLzV4tirE-ZxDfA/4r6/w-bgnRmHS7Ci0CeQIFt0JA/h6/h001.10QpEZft50_8TfjX-el4C84jOOn5SUVML3AxGmLUejY).
* * *
★ Iran Watch
## Trump Moves to Silence the Guns in Lebanon as Iran Talks Teeter
President Trump announced he had personally brokered a halt to the fighting between Israel and Iran-backed Hezbollah, saying he spoke with both sides and that **"all shooting will stop."** The move came as Tehran claimed it was suspending indirect negotiations with Washington over Israel's expanding operations in Lebanon.The Situation
* ▸ Trump said no U.S. or Israeli troops would enter Beirut, and that forces already en route had been **turned back**.
* ▸ He insisted talks with Iran were still moving at a **"rapid pace"** , brushing off Tehran's claim that negotiations had collapsed.
* ▸ The **Strait of Hormuz** — the chokepoint for roughly a fifth of the world's oil — remains the central pressure point in the standoff.

The DebateSkeptics note that fighting continued along the Israel-Lebanon border even after the announcement, and Prime Minister Netanyahu signaled Israel's military would keep operating in southern Lebanon as planned. But Trump showed no urgency to chase a deal, telling reporters that if Iran doesn't want to talk, that's fine by him — and reminding NATO allies who depend on Gulf oil far more than America does.Read the full story at [CBS News](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/ss/c/u001.SfPhhFqVdCCzAqIAosiI_PMx2qeeRMJxkulIYhfBCSXn0YojNvqwoqGfGsQD903JqQxIeo-8W92Rr0gRGiPcaECO6Kopo66a8ISUaI5nTjkUP3E9TvBPnI6MRA9h6Ne8GrG3bdi9jKfTybtkA8TEXn5tkw-qgjZSdkq4jR03OOqh6ezNRowpdCgsG-c9lq-TIXYNxyAgT5hnhuut4TcUFB8vFcIXOdRqtTLW9JnpE2b-XECE2z5kXAtPa3GynbAQzZGHhOmNAO-CGFmDbu9xZ3M_iLsqVtwOz4W6jkK3I22D_Bk3KwBOWNuSKzVCmFutOHy6ADLoVxiX2SDA4EWQYw/4r6/w-bgnRmHS7Ci0CeQIFt0JA/h7/h001.CLn4bMBGM_SncKuL1BdakcbPOqj0uVAkWMbYHPqIowQ).
* * *
★ The Economy
## Pump Pain Persists — But Ceasefire Hopes Offer a Lifeline
The Middle East standoff is still being felt at every gas station in America. The national average sat around **$4.26 a gallon** heading into this week — up dramatically from under $3 before the conflict — as the closure of the Strait of Hormuz keeps a lid on global oil supply.The Numbers
* ▸ U.S. gasoline futures climbed back above **$3.10 a gallon** in early June amid the supply crunch.
* ▸ Energy exports through the key Gulf chokepoint have been at a near-standstill since early March, draining global inventories at a record pace.
* ▸ Even so, Wall Street has stayed cool — the **S &P; 500** notched fresh record highs as investors bet on a resolution.

Why It MattersReports point to a **60-day memorandum** that would extend the current ceasefire and reopen the flow of crude through Hormuz within a month — a deal that could finally bring relief at the pump. America's status as the world's largest oil producer is the cushion softening the blow, but families filling up still want the squeeze to end.Read the full story at [Fortune](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/ss/c/u001.helAEltPsJerhr4Tfhlii0w6A2BcDKZrphBJq_5fq9v4H-D2rTIB3g37prqj64kb6FGNsJvt_Lv9MMfZFr6SMBSr-uQMe5whfVPDvDsczcigTkasaaYWCDlP9ZbaKDSP8uuyiW8bg8VgpcpY4u_8PPnM85q07O1ToFlmsas5mldOQkehDD8eiXncvtBmqdtSat_u8P0g4eqIzIp3pKGLsvzUUTlHzis9YCfUJIFkBiinW6rZLvJK3XYSkJe__gyZ1Kwt0P_z5hxizjchRB-xDemVwED7LoLxhEflftdFQoY/4r6/w-bgnRmHS7Ci0CeQIFt0JA/h8/h001.aFkM2qtVUUGWLi4Wip4Mldja5FHv0x9gwuUxl6_jV04).⚡ The Bottom LineVoters from California to Iowa just showed they're hungry for fighters who put affordability and the forgotten American first — establishment résumés be damned. Overseas, Trump is leaning on leverage instead of begging for a deal, while the path to lower gas prices runs straight through the Strait of Hormuz. **The map is shifting, and it's shifting toward the people who feel the cost of living every single day.** "The truth isn't conservative or liberal. name: Defenders of Wildlife
subject: Heroes in American Conservation: Fall in Love with the Woods Gifford Pinchot
body:
Meet the Father of American Forestry and Conservation!
Meet the Father of American Forestry and Conservation!
| [](https://support.defenders.org/s/5583681/38SyG9Xl)
---
| | |
---
#
|
---
[](https://support.defenders.org/s/5583682/38SyG9Xl)
---
#
Meet American Conservation Hero Gifford Pinchot
---
| | |
---
#
#### **_Who is he?_**
Gifford Pinchot (1865–1946) is often called the “Father of American Forestry and Conservation” because of his unrelenting work and advocacy for the protection of U.S. forests. He spent most of his free time growing up in his favorite place: the woods. He was the first known professional American forester and quickly rose in the Interior Department of Agriculture, where Forestry was housed and, eventually, the U.S. Forest Service was created.
#
In fact, Pinchot was the first Chief of the U.S. Forest Service (Republican, 1905-1910) under Theodore Roosevelt. During his time here, the number of forest reserves and protected areas nearly tripled.
#
He is also credited with giving us the sentiment that public lands belong to us, the American people – that we own them and are all invested in in them.
#
|
---
| | |
---
#
#### **_Did Pinchot preserve forests for wildlife?_**
Pinchot viewed all nature as a resource to sustainably tap into and saw how forests were important habitat for animals.
#
Grizzly bears, Canada lynx, bats, woodpeckers, salamanders and owls – many of whom are listed under the Endangered Species Act – have key habitat in our national forests. Defenders of Wildlife is actively working to continue the protection of our forests, including keeping nearly one-third of them [**free from harmful road development.**](https://support.defenders.org/s/5583683/38SyG9Xl)
#
|
---
| | |
---
#
#### **_How can you become a conservation hero?_**
Like Pinchot, you can spark a love for nature through exploring local woods, parks and trails. You also have the power to protect the forests and nature around you. Our public lands belong to you, the public! Tell your elected officials you would like to continue to see our national forests protected for generations of wildlife and people to enjoy. And, of course, [**follow Defenders**](https://support.defenders.org/s/5583684/38SyG9Xl) to learn about and engage in more wildlife conservation issues.
#
|
---
###
_A note on our Heroes in American Conservation series: Our country has a long and complex history, populated with high-profile figures whose views may have been complicated or divisive in their time as well as ours. We present these conservationists in the interest of creating a greater understanding of the roots of the American conservation movement, and to inspire you to make your own contribution to ongoing conversations about how we preserve our wild world._
#
---
| | |
---
#
|
---
|

| | | Peter,

What I wouldn't give for one more love letter from Charlie.

One more handwritten note left beside my coffee before he rushed out the door.

One more folded piece of paper on my pillow before he had an early flight.

One more moment where he intentionally set aside the noise of the world just to remind me that I was loved.

About this time last year, Charlie and I sat together on-stage at the Women's Leadership Summit (WLS), answering questions from young women about marriage, family, faith, raising children, and the kind of future they hoped to have one day.
---
[](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=170af6e052814f3c85776d61d662409b&_e=JAAUa7VsxLSWyDRW3R0n_aMHbc95qLMmmPXE5DV_SmwzHEG9SHI7oSEX-VJGi-dl7GD8D9n7hOQmVwoWuTHG9DsFHbHwPPwYP_m1fFyDP3P60ez4s3JwjKx72048GFt9GAfqqNrXMXFSO8tUs4k9afR_PmutVL4wADQHx8VQ4WvK0hD1BZx4zaRJvgEXn7WtMpHXiYjgN0GmHkUSPmm12mPRWQrJYFMEBHZxwW88G1KkHOss-Fo7b0hdXR4WmDWfED5cAhpQMCWnjRHyH1ers-37TmdXE-CVt_Thj9knG2vSt3UeuOjoOdhbY15tsbRsmlf6BiMOLO4O-e9wlPIXb5WHVvTdlL0RcbNZhtMj9-Mhv2jtjtUWxERMFSZP7eAqw4hxjrZq4GZRRYO__QGtIiaYFjk5jvFnaSLsWvwHGimveNqPDCVU0phBbCQGnyleO-5hChss7m6xHUYazwbaGRUQVURm6cMsR17mnJcd62umqPD-n2aiMw-ilUU1AnIHkit3_FO-jkkrSLe7NwhMik4nf07hBY6GR1v6BdLkZqeHn78WgBmI-wdm_iS_xX3OGU70IKahi5RvnQU9_U2bvoBRNx3zeGjQ6ZbqYW9QIgxYuAbAcHNOicdpFonTyIjLYflz-X3CTIu6AwSG2lEaafD6zYMfEugun4ZkcDLopJOd4ms_PquCgJF2zwj7zok2Xsk38HXBcjf6WNGh1qJYV-cMvrNtGPd38yJAmq_SSTYEoCZf09OSN-NqVphKiqag)

Somewhere during that conversation, I mentioned the notes he would write to me.

They were one of the many quiet ways Charlie loved me.

I shared that he would write them whenever he had a moment while he honored the Sabbath.

_He never missed one. _

Sometimes they were only a few sentences, but they carried such a deep reverence about them. He'd hand me words that felt sacred.

I saved every single one of those letters.
---
[](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=170af6e052814f3c85776d61d662409b&_e=JAAUa7VsxLSWyDRW3R0n_aMHbc95qLMmmPXE5DV_SmwzHEG9SHI7oSEX-VJGi-dl7GD8D9n7hOQmVwoWuTHG9DsFHbHwPPwYP_m1fFyDP3P60ez4s3JwjKx72048GFt9GAfqqNrXMXFSO8tUs4k9afR_PmutVL4wADQHx8VQ4WvK0hD1BZx4zaRJvgEXn7WtMpHXiYjgN0GmHkUSPmm12mPRWQrJYFMEBHZxwW88G1KkHOss-Fo7b0hdXR4WmDWfED5cAhpQMCWnjRHyH1ers8bYrRVcnEsnMd8CJ6OR6YfSKIa3LRWWy4RpaqOs8Kd89E87gKJqXELo0YSOhC9UhWumUOZOwVRo6_enVoh_sqxDBYudP3QOyzTIvj6xt7-w7hmI8R8JElwxzBjsAYQKajb7dLN3LIdoOs0RqVc3JRvz4hXeBW5e2jDDWlfhp0YmqKC3BcLDVENANIX5Ogl8q1q8GgljyFog7dlwXoH6IOHIxzL8P_LEpD7z9D-C5PG_G690as78_WUc_h2h4N55MVHJG3wztkMz2Zk3j0k3ghdXaZRqmOagi1KRHwkoCIU_0qUiHiqqmSgFjjTDB-dyZJokFdLMLU3O4RU6qGWiArV8x2ywZ3cjq1NpNlyYnT6SHlP4mgPCNdskrtoSlZ9PeVfu6tqA4DUe7XrIB7THt4xW8QtBLaaei9J7145BelhTd1XnGAyebg1OOAUTI3vPp_J7yMeOQUaYUdF4AaL9ZsL5hzGTCzNLJg2TjoMxfMkR)

Charlie knew how much those little notes meant to me, and now I treasure them in a way I never could have understood at the time.

I hold onto every word he left for me.

And looking back, I think about the young women in the room listening to us that night at the Women's Leadership Summit.

Because so many of those young women were longing for something this culture keeps trying to convince them no longer matters.

A strong family. A faithful marriage. Children raised in a home filled with purpose and love.

A life rooted in God instead of endless striving and the empty pursuit of self.

And honestly, Peter, I think that ache runs much deeper than most people realize.

I see it constantly when I meet young women across the country.

So many feel exhausted by the pressure to chase an image of success that leaves them anxious, disconnected, and lonely.

They've been told that fulfillment comes from constant achievement... endless comparison... putting themselves first.

But as I said last year, the enemy has a way of disguising bondage as empowerment.

I think that's part of why so many young women are drawn to the Women's Leadership Summit in the first place.

Because for one weekend, thousands of young women come together and realize they are not alone for wanting a different kind of life.

They meet other young women who still love God, still believe family matters, and still want meaningful lives rooted in faith and purpose.
---
[](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=170af6e052814f3c85776d61d662409b&_e=JAAUa7VsxLSWyDRW3R0n_aMHbc95qLMmmPXE5DV_SmwzHEG9SHI7oSEX-VJGi-dl7GD8D9n7hOQmVwoWuTHG9DsFHbHwPPwYP_m1fFyDP3P60ez4s3JwjKx72048GFt9GAfqqNrXMXFSO8tUs4k9afR_PmutVL4wADQHx8VQ4WvK0hD1BZx4zaRJvgEXn7WtMpHXiYjgN0GmHkUSPmm12mPRWQrJYFMEBHZxwW88G1KkHOss-Fo7b0hdXR4WmDWfED5cAhpQMCWnjRHyH1ers6WbV2meiDProEd41FzIP4xualQSI_bxff2PtHdCgv3wcXJ9zIi9F3QwhMYlVOGyKbssE6lUZLCPHA76sL4VPkxrHR1Awt40p2SoBM7rAl1Yg4BdY48z4KBPkxSN2GA6q7b4wRHQZBifmMSfOUCrWN-5I9VFqbjccNP_uE4YfWBbsoT2Ep0zsTbv_bVkBE8DdjzhYdaK8d6m4Cysf0-jMwCFuIjshUVxbi09dLZFnemfXrbG5ivvC177Ul6e6zdh9T8NHOWiWO1aJ8fLhzeCtEEvmZngbOah9pCWZWw3J9WtPpAu0GvPgqavtbJGpedYxBbZJdPg0nJ1XWBg4KYYq9RhEcam6dMN9WDhEWUMcXT8apPS2DSqxTMtKStyqgJFn2VtvsIv6QxygArbMB-qkfSghG111Tsi61Jv_-6YZ5Td4eHg_oelBArk1PoZYisowjZGyfJH0wwbCq-1Ar_YNLxo-JWGDpW874h03PzndzzL)

Last year during our question-and-answer session at the Women's Leadership Summit, one young woman walked up to the microphone... and Charlie recognized her immediately.

Before she could even ask her question, Charlie's face lit up with a huge smile as he said, _" Hey! So... you're getting married!" _

The room burst into cheers as she smiled and nodded her head.

And then Charlie reminded everyone why he recognized her in the first place.

The year before, she had stood at the mic and asked him a simple question:

_" How do I meet a husband?" _

A year later, she came back to WLS engaged.

I smile thinking about how excited everyone in that room was for her.

I see moments like that every year at the Women's Leadership Summit. And after I leave, I always carry home a deep sense of hope about this next generation of young women.

Not because they have everything figured out.

But because so many of them are still searching for what is true, and for who God designed them to be.

Revival is not going to come through louder politicians or more influencers.

It's going to come through the living rooms of mothers who pray with their children, pray over their children, and love their husbands. And through bold actions of unshakeable devotion to Jesus Christ.

I believe the way a woman loves her family, raises her children, serves others, and walks with God leaves a mark on the world far greater than most people will ever realize.

That's why this event matters so deeply to me.

And when I think back on my own life, I know how true that is.

Before I met Charlie, I was not dreaming about marriage, motherhood, and building a family.

But when I met the right man, everything shifted. Everything changed.

And before doors open in San Antonio for the Women's Leadership Summit this June, I just want to thank you for helping make this event possible year after year.

Thank you for helping us continue pouring into these young women.

Thank you for helping carry forward a mission that changes so many lives -- including mine.

I truly cannot wait to see what God does through this next generation of young women.
---
| | | **For Charlie,**** ****Erika Kirk** CEO & ChairTurning Point USA

**P.S.** Looking back now, I think some of the moments that leave the deepest mark on your life are the ones you almost don't realize are sacred while you're living them.

A love note on Saturday. A prayer before bed. A husband asking how he can better serve you.

You don't realize until much later that those small acts of love and faithfulness were quietly building something eternal inside your home.

I read all of Charlie's love letters even slower now.

And as I read his words, the weight on my heart reminds me that we were never promised gray hair and rocking chairs -- even though we assumed it was guaranteed.

Charlie and I built our marriage around the kind of covenant described in Ephesians 5 -- rooted in faith, sacrifice, service, and putting Christ at the center of our home.

And it's another reason why Charlie cared so deeply about our nation's young people -- both men and women.

He wanted them to know there is still meaning to be found in building a beautiful life rooted in the things that actually last.

Get married.
Have children.
Build a legacy.
Pass down your values.
Pursue the eternal.
Seek true joy.

That kind of life may not be what this culture celebrates anymore... but I still believe with my whole heart that it is the life so many young women are quietly searching for.

As the Women's Leadership Summit approaches, I'm deeply grateful for people like you who help us continue to create a place where they can encounter that kind of faith, encouragement, and purpose.

From the bottom of my heart, thank you.

clean_body: Charlie never missed writing a single one | | | | | | | Peter, What I wouldn't give for one more love letter from Charlie. One more handwritten note left beside my coffee before he rushed out the door. One more folded piece of paper on my pillow before he had an early flight. One more moment where he intentionally set aside the noise of the world just to remind me that I was loved. About this time last year, Charlie and I sat together on-stage at the Women's Leadership Summit (WLS), answering questions from young women about marriage, family, faith, raising children, and the kind of future they hoped to have one day. Somewhere during that conversation, I mentioned the notes he would write to me. They were one of the many quiet ways Charlie loved me. I shared that he would write them whenever he had a moment while he honored the Sabbath. He never missed one. Sometimes they were only a few sentences, but they carried such a deep reverence about them. He'd hand me words that felt sacred. I saved every single one of those letters. Charlie knew how much those little notes meant to me, and now I treasure them in a way I never could have understood at the time. I hold onto every word he left for me. And looking back, I think about the young women in the room listening to us that night at the Women's Leadership Summit. Because so many of those young women were longing for something this culture keeps trying to convince them no longer matters. A strong family. A faithful marriage. Children raised in a home filled with purpose and love. A life rooted in God instead of endless striving and the empty pursuit of self. And honestly, Peter, I think that ache runs much deeper than most people realize. I see it constantly when I meet young women across the country. So many feel exhausted by the pressure to chase an image of success that leaves them anxious, disconnected, and lonely. They've been told that fulfillment comes from constant achievement... endless comparison... putting themselves first. But as I said last year, the enemy has a way of disguising bondage as empowerment. I think that's part of why so many young women are drawn to the Women's Leadership Summit in the first place. Because for one weekend, thousands of young women come together and realize they are not alone for wanting a different kind of life. They meet other young women who still love God, still believe family matters, and still want meaningful lives rooted in faith and purpose. Last year during our question-and-answer session at the Women's Leadership Summit, one young woman walked up to the microphone... and Charlie recognized her immediately. Before she could even ask her question, Charlie's face lit up with a huge smile as he said, " Hey! So... you're getting married!" The room burst into cheers as she smiled and nodded her head. And then Charlie reminded everyone why he recognized her in the first place. The year before, she had stood at the mic and asked him a simple question: " How do I meet a husband?" A year later, she came back to WLS engaged. I smile thinking about how excited everyone in that room was for her. I see moments like that every year at the Women's Leadership Summit. And after I leave, I always carry home a deep sense of hope about this next generation of young women. Not because they have everything figured out. But because so many of them are still searching for what is true, and for who God designed them to be. Revival is not going to come through louder politicians or more influencers. It's going to come through the living rooms of mothers who pray with their children, pray over their children, and love their husbands. And through bold actions of unshakeable devotion to Jesus Christ. I believe the way a woman loves her family, raises her children, serves others, and walks with God leaves a mark on the world far greater than most people will ever realize. That's why this event matters so deeply to me. And when I think back on my own life, I know how true that is. Before I met Charlie, I was not dreaming about marriage, motherhood, and building a family. But when I met the right man, everything shifted. Everything changed. And before doors open in San Antonio for the Women's Leadership Summit this June, I just want to thank you for helping make this event possible year after year. Thank you for helping us continue pouring into these young women. Thank you for helping carry forward a mission that changes so many lives -- including mine. I truly cannot wait to see what God does through this next generation of young women. | | | For Charlie, Erika Kirk CEO & ChairTurning Point USA P.S. Looking back now, I think some of the moments that leave the deepest mark on your life are the ones you almost don't realize are sacred while you're living them. A love note on Saturday. A prayer before bed. A husband asking how he can better serve you. You don't realize until much later that those small acts of love and faithfulness were quietly building something eternal inside your home. I read all of Charlie's love letters even slower now. And as I read his words, the weight on my heart reminds me that we were never promised gray hair and rocking chairs -- even though we assumed it was guaranteed. Charlie and I built our marriage around the kind of covenant described in Ephesians 5 -- rooted in faith, sacrifice, service, and putting Christ at the center of our home. And it's another reason why Charlie cared so deeply about our nation's young people -- both men and women. He wanted them to know there is still meaning to be found in building a beautiful life rooted in the things that actually last. Get married. Have children. Build a legacy. Pass down your values. Pursue the eternal. Seek true joy. That kind of life may not be what this culture celebrates anymore... but I still believe with my whole heart that it is the life so many young women are quietly searching for. As the Women's Leadership Summit approaches, I'm deeply grateful for people like you who help us continue to create a place where they can encounter that kind of faith, encouragement, and purpose. From the bottom of my heart, thank you. And with the doors opening in a matter of days, if you'd like to help one more young woman find her calling, 4940 East Beverly Road Phoenix, Arizona 85044
